metadata.title: Resilience, Resistance and Retreat: Strategies to Manage Online Violence Against Women in the Workplace
metadata.description:
Women in journalism in public-facing roles are notably targeted by gendered harassment and abuse during
the course of their work, with existing research demonstrating the scope, scale and impact of online violence
against women in journalism both in the UK and internationally.

Reach Plc is the largest commercial publisher in the UK, with more than more than 1,500 journalists working
across more than 120 brands in the UK, Republic of Ireland and the USA. In 2021 the company appointed an
Online Safety Editor to work with journalists who were reporting significant levels of online abuse and
harassment.

From January 2022, all online safety reports made by journalists at Reach have been recorded, producing a
rich data set of more than 550 events to date. Report data includes the category of harm alongside the
platform and method of delivery.

This research analyses the data set to find that reports made by women are of a higher volume and are more
frequently categorised as higher risk than those made by men. It finds the events targeting women are more
likely to include sexually violent or misogynistic gendered language, references to body parts, body image
and eating, dehumanising language such as animalistic terms and is more likely to refer directly to the given
name of the journalist. Intersectional abuse referencing ethnicity and religion is also more likely in events
affecting women.

The research also includes follow-up qualitative testimony from women journalists affected by online harm,
with insights into their recovery from traumatic online harm, their coping strategies and how they continue
to work professionally following harmful events.

The research seeks to identify transferable protective and coping strategies and also to identify gaps in
support, legislation and technology.

Due to the source material and subject, this research is presented as a journalistic work.

metadata.title: A Holistic Market Research Analysis of Carbon-Negative Fuel  Systems embedding Decision-Making Procedures
metadata.description:
The document is a short paper for ICDSST 2026 is authored by REACH Innovation together with several European research partners and presents the Market and Competitive Research Analysis (MCRA) developed within the Horizon Europe project NET‑Fuels.

The paper explains how decision-support methodologies (SWOT, PESTEL, Porter’s Five Forces) were integrated into a structured workflow to evaluate and position NET‑Fuels’ carbon‑negative fuel technologies within the current technological and regulatory landscape.

metadata.title: Participatory activities good practices in the field of cultural heritage (REACH project)
metadata.description: The REACH repository of good practices comprises over a hundred and twenty records of European and extra European participatory activities in the field of cultural heritage, with an emphasis on small-scale, localised examples, but including also larger collaborative projects and global or distributed online initiatives. Located in over twenty different countries, the activities showcased here cover a wide variety of topics and themes, from urban, rural and institutional heritage to indigenous and minority heritage; from preservation, and management to use and re-use of cultural heritage. This easy-to-use collection of good practices offers professionals, practitioners, researchers and citizens useful information about activities which could be transferred, adapted or replicated in new contexts.

metadata.title: Proposed New CO2 Emissions Mitigation Mechanism
metadata.description:
MM, the new CO2 Emissions Mitigation Mechanism (Mitigation Mechanism) proposed in this work, is the CO2 mitigation program assisting the countries to reach the 1.5°C-2.0°C global warming limit in the year 2100.

Considering climate justice, the countries which will not reduce their CO2 emissions to the limit in a specific year will buy carbon credits. The new CO2 Emissions Mitigation Mechanism introduces an efficient way to buy carbon credits and an efficient way to use carbon credits.

This work proposes a procedure to guarantee constant carbon credit price, known in advance. This procedure does not require the involvement of carbon traders, reducing the time between the creation of emissions reduction and the actual money transfer to the project participants.

The carbon credits issued by the operating organization will be sold to the countries which did not reduce their CO2 emissions to the required limit in the specific year. These carbon credits will have a constant price without a time limit, known in advance publicly.

The money received from the buying country will be used as an incentive for CO2 mitigation projects and will be transferred directly to the project participant instead of carbon credits. Considering the 50$ carbon credit cost the maximum cumulative cost of the carbon credits proposed in this work will be 0.61% of the world cumulative GDP in the period 2025-2100. The maximum yearly cost of the carbon credits will be in the year 2037, 0.70% of the world’s GDP.

metadata.title: D6.3 - 1st. Communication, Dissemination and Exploitation Report
metadata.description:
This document (D6.3) is a follow-up of the Communication, Dissemination and Exploitation (CD&E) planning report (D6.2) delivered in Month 6. D6.3 describes related tasks and activities carried out by the relevant partners of NET-Fuels project team covering the period of 30/04/2023 to 29/02/2024 (M6-M16).
This report is a ‘living document’ that represents, for all interested parties, a reference for the communication, dissemination and exploitation strategy and activities of the project. The timeline for these reports submitted via the EC portal is indicated below:
 D6.2 - Dissemination, exploitation and communication plan (M6, April 2023)
 D6.3 - First dissemination, exploitation and communication report (M16, February 2024) (current)
 D6.4 - Second dissemination, exploitation and communication report (M36, October 2025)

Main Purpose of D6.3: A comprehensive Communication, Dissemination, and Exploitation (CD&E) plan is fundamental to ensure maximum impact of the NET-Fuels project by supporting the outputs from the project (e.g.: deliverables and key-exploitable results (KERs). Identifying target audiences and creating tailored information to engage and
share with these audiences will put the necessary steps and actions in place to facilitate the future (post-project) maturation of the technology to pre-commercial scale and, ultimately, to full commercial implementation.
